name: Grammar of spoken academic interaction
scope: Features and accuracy priorities of spoken academic English (heads and tails, ellipsis, vague language, discourse markers, clause chaining) for seminars, tutorials and presentations.

name: Genitive and noun-modifier choices
scope: Choosing between 's, of-phrases and noun + noun modifiers (the study's aim / the aim of the study / study aim), including inanimate genitives and the myth that they are wrong.

name: Unaccusative and ergative verbs
scope: Verbs such as occur, happen, emerge, increase and change that describe events without an agent or alternate between transitive and intransitive use; avoiding *was happened and *was emerged.

name: Explaining concepts and readings to peers
scope: Mediating a concept, text or dataset for classmates: simplifying, exemplifying, checking understanding and drawing on shared languages, in seminars, study groups and peer teaching.

name: Short-format research pitches
scope: Three-minute thesis and elevator-style pitches that compress a project into a single accessible narrative for mixed audiences.

name: Extended source-based project
scope: An independently researched essay or report of several thousand words on a self-chosen focus in the learner's field, developed through proposal, annotated sources, drafts and tutorials, often with a reflective commentary; the capstone of many pre-sessional and foundation EAP courses.

name: Whose knowledge is cited
scope: Recognising that citation and indexing practices shape whose knowledge becomes visible, including the dominance of English-language, Global North and highly indexed sources, and making deliberate, justified citation choices.

name: Doctoral progression and confirmation reviews
scope: Confirmation, upgrade and annual progression reports and the accompanying oral review: summarising progress, revising questions and design, presenting preliminary findings, planning, and responding to panel questions.

name: Thesis by publication
scope: Framing chapters, linking narratives and co-authorship statements that turn stand-alone papers into one coherent thesis argument.

name: Writing systematic and scoping reviews
scope: Writing the protocol and report of a systematic, scoping or other structured review in any discipline: registration, transparent search and selection reporting, appraisal and synthesis, following reporting guidance such as PRISMA 2020.

name: Wording survey and interview questions
scope: Writing clear, neutral, single-focus questionnaire items, response scales and interview prompts, and piloting them for comprehension with the intended participants.

name: Teaching, demonstrating and marking as a doctoral researcher
scope: Communicating as a graduate teaching assistant or demonstrator: explaining concepts and procedures, questioning, managing small-group discussion, giving spoken and written feedback, and handling student queries.

name: Funding, fellowship and grant applications
scope: Case for support, lay summary, impact statement and track-record sections for studentships, travel grants and early-career fellowships.

name: Participating in conferences
scope: Asking and answering questions from the floor, chairing a session, and networking and following up contacts at conferences and research seminars.

name: Personal statements for postgraduate study and funding
scope: Statements of purpose and scholarship applications that show fit, motivation and capability with evidence.

name: Examiners' reports and thesis corrections
scope: Interpreting examiners' reports and viva outcomes, turning them into a corrections plan, and documenting the changes made.

name: From thesis to articles
scope: Turning thesis chapters into journal articles, or integrating published papers into a thesis: re-scoping the argument for a journal readership, compressing the literature and methods, and managing self-plagiarism rules.

name: Open research practices and statements
scope: Writing the texts open-research practices require: preprints and versions, preregistration and registered reports, data and code availability statements, and other disclosure statements.

name: Assistive technology and study adjustments
scope: Using assistive and accessibility technologies (text-to-speech, dictation, screen readers, reading and planning supports) and institutional adjustments as legitimate academic practice, within assessment rules.

name: Informal academic interaction and networking
scope: Small talk and relationship-building with peers, lab colleagues and staff around teaching and at departmental events, moving between informal and academic talk.

name: Applications and interviews for placements and graduate roles
scope: Cover letters, competency-based answers and interview talk that translate academic experience into evidence for employers.

name: Translingual writing and code-meshing
scope: Understanding translingual approaches in which writers deliberately bring other languages or Englishes into academic texts, when and how this is accepted, and how to negotiate it with readers and assessors.

name: Score reports, validity and test choice
scope: Reading proficiency-test score reports (overall and component scores, retake and combined-sitting rules where they exist), judging whether they meet a requirement, and choosing a test.

name: Laboratory notebooks and research records
scope: Keeping contemporaneous, reproducible lab, computational or fieldwork records that meet research-integrity and data-management expectations.

name: Writing clinical reasoning
scope: Making assessment, problem identification and intervention reasoning explicit in nursing, pharmacy and allied-health assignments, linked to evidence and professional standards.

name: Care plans
scope: Care plans and care-planning assignments that move from holistic assessment to prioritised, person-centred needs, goals, evidence-based interventions and evaluation.

name: Language and genres of accounting and finance
scope: Financial statement commentary, audit and valuation reports, and the evaluative and hedged language of financial analysis in finance and accounting assessments.

name: Consultancy and client project reports
scope: Client-facing reports for live or simulated consultancy projects: problem framing, evidence-based recommendations, implementation and reflection, for a client and an academic marker.

name: Mooting and oral legal argument
scope: Preparing and delivering oral legal submissions in moots and assessed advocacy: skeleton arguments, ordering grounds, citing authority orally and answering judicial questions.

name: Legal research and dissertation writing
scope: Planning and writing a law dissertation: choosing and justifying a doctrinal, socio-legal, comparative or theoretical method, building a research question, and structuring sustained legal argument.

name: Psychology research reports
scope: APA-style empirical reports in psychology: hypotheses, participants and materials, statistical reporting conventions and the discipline's stance conventions.

name: Education and TESOL practice genres
scope: Lesson plans with rationale, teaching-practice reflections, materials evaluations and small-scale classroom research reports in education and TESOL programmes.

name: Practice-based research and exegesis
scope: The exegesis or critical commentary that accompanies practice-based research in art, design and performance, situating the practice in its field and articulating its contribution.
